touches.text: The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.
feedback: where a component's failing findings go (the -2-> edge). WHY: a finding that goes nowhere teaches nothing. USERS: the inspectors.
No rule refuses a route spelled as a keyword where a finding is built: the old charter clause asking for one measured the wrong thing, and is retired (Q#116). -amm
